title: Computing a PracticePay Patient Financing Returned-Payment-Fee Relief
content:
**What is considered.** The returned payment considered is the plan's latest returned-payment entry by return date, the one recorded first where two share that date; its fee is the returned-payment fee entry that names it, the payment that came back is the payment entry it reverses, and that payment's due date is the installment due date that payment entry names.

**Replaced and cleared.** The payment that came back has been replaced after the return when it was credited toward a monthly due date, the plan's next due date, its oldest unpaid due date, is later than that due date, and the latest payment entry credited toward that due date, the one recorded first where two share that date, is dated after the return date and has not come back, no returned-payment entry naming it; that latest payment's date is the replacement date, and the replacement has cleared once 3 calendar days have passed since the replacement date.

**When a relief is owed.** A returned-payment-fee relief is owed only when the replacement has cleared, today is no later than the fee waiver request window after the fee's assessment date, fewer than the plan's courtesy waivers per 12 months have been granted on the plan within the last 12 months, and the fee carries no waiver entry yet; otherwise nothing is relieved. In this schedule the courtesy waivers granted within the last 12 months are those dated fewer than 12 whole months before the relief date, a month being whole once the relief date's day of the month has reached the entry's day of the month. The request window and the number of courtesy waivers are the per-plan figures in the PracticePay Patient Financing fee schedule.

**Amount.** The returned-payment-fee relief is the returned-payment fee in full, rounded half up to the nearest cent. Where a rule of the returned-payment-fee relief schedule sets a relief size or a share, the relief size takes the place of the full fee, every share multiplies it, all shares applying together, the product is never more than the part of the fee not already waived, and it is rounded half up to the nearest cent once, at the end. A returned-payment-fee relief that works out to 0.00 is not owed, and nothing is booked for it.

## Checklist of conditions, with a hypothetical case (relief date 20 June)

| Condition | Hypothetical record | Met |
|---|---|---|
| latest returned payment | a payment of 150.00 USD credited toward the 1 June due date came back on 5 June; a fee of 20.00 USD was assessed on 5 June | — |
| next due date later than that due date | next due date 1 July | yes |
| latest payment toward 1 June dated after the return and not come back | 9 June, not come back | yes; replacement date 9 June |
| cleared | 11 days since 9 June | yes |
| within the request window after the fee's assessment | 15 days after 5 June | yes |
| courtesy waivers in the last 12 months below the plan's number | none | yes |
| no waiver entry on the fee yet | none | yes |
| relief | the fee in full | 20.00 USD |
